research:
I've gathered enough context and am writing it up now. Note: some search results were dated after 2026-09-22. I excluded them as the exercise requires.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on Yahoo Finance ^FTSE daily closes. Code-collected data puts the latest close at **10,739.00 on 2026-09-21**, which is the base value. I could not fetch a live Yahoo page or a news report giving the 2026-09-22 close.
- Code baseline (empirical 8-trading-day returns over 3 years, last year weighted double), converted to % change from 10,739:
  - p5 -2.44%, p10 -1.78%, p25 -0.67%
  - p50 +0.54%
  - p75 +1.63%, p90 +2.62%, p95 +3.26%

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The window covers 9 trading sessions (Sep 22 to Oct 2). The base close is known, and the outcome depends entirely on future moves.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-17: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on a 6-3 vote. Greene, Mann and Pill voted for a rise to 4%. The guidance turned more hawkish, with inflation risks "tilted to the upside", and a November hike is described as live. The next MPC meeting is 2026-11-05. [Cambridge Currencies](https://cambridgecurrencies.com/next-bank-of-england-interest-rate-decision/?nb=1), [Forex Fundamentals](https://forexfundamentals.com/economic-calendar/boe/2026-09-17)
- 2026-09-16: The Fed reportedly hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote. The dot plot reportedly showed one more hike in 2026. US stocks reportedly turned lower during Chair Warsh's press conference as yields and the dollar rose. These are secondary trading-site sources I could not confirm. [Admiral Markets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/fed-raised-interest-rates), [MetaTradingClub](https://www.metatradingclub.com/?p=25647), [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-september-2026)
- 2026-09-10: The ECB raised rates 25bp (deposit rate 2.50%) and revised its 2027-28 inflation projections up. The FTSE fell that day as Brent hit $106 a barrel. One report puts the close at 10,608.92. ABF dropped after a Primark sales warning. [HL/Sharecast](https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/market-reports/london-close-ftse-falls-amid-inflation-worries-as-brent-hits-$106-a-barrel), [BBN Times](https://www.bbntimes.com/financial/ftse-100-today-london-stocks-fall-to-10-608-92-as-ecb-delivers-rate-hike-amid-inflation-concerns)
- 2026-08-31: The FTSE 100 ended August roughly flat at about 10,767, held back by weakness in tobacco stocks. [interactive investor](https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/uk-stock-market-winners-and-losers-august-2026-ii540146)
- 2026-08-28: A snapshot shows the index at 10,824.26. [finanzen.ch](https://styles.finanzen.ch/index/analysen/ftse_100?p=64)
- Taken together: the global backdrop is a tightening cycle (Fed, ECB, BoE leaning hawkish) with oil above $100. From about 10,609 on Sep 10 the index recovered to 10,739 by Sep 21, close to where it ended August.

## 4. Base rates
- The empirical distribution above has a median of about +0.5% over 8 trading days, with an interquartile range of about -0.7% to +1.6%. The 5-95% band is roughly -2.4% to +3.3%. That implies a standard deviation of about 1.7%.
- The FTSE has moved in a fairly tight range for months: about 10,650 in early July, 10,738 on Jul 24, about 10,945 at end-July (monthly figure), about 10,767 at end-August, about 10,609 on Sep 10 and 10,739 on Sep 21. [Upstox](https://upstox.com/global-indices/ftse-100/), [digrin](https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/%5EFTSE/price)
- The 2026 trend is broadly sideways after the index broke 10,000 in January. [MarketScreener](https://in.marketscreener.com/news/ftse-100-tops-10-000-as-starts-new-year-in-style-ce7e59d9dc8df422)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the FTSE 100 level for this window.
- poundf.co.uk publishes model-generated daily "predictions" for late September (for example 10,535 for Sep 23, with a very wide range). These are low quality. [poundf](https://poundf.co.uk/ftse)
- Before the meeting, prediction markets priced a BoE hold at about 76%, and the hold happened. [Polyguana](https://polyguana.com/market/2661519)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (Sep 22 to Oct 2)
- **Late September:** US PCE inflation data. After a hawkish Fed, an inflation surprise matters more than usual.
- **Sep 30:** Quarter-end rebalancing, final UK Q2 GDP, and around this date flash euro-area CPI for September. Euro-area inflation drew attention after the ECB hike.
- **Oct 1-2:** Global manufacturing PMIs, then US September payrolls on Oct 2, the last session in the window.
- **Ongoing:** Oil prices with Brent above $100, which helps the FTSE's energy-heavy weighting but hurts the wider risk mood. Also gilt yields and sterling: a stronger pound tends to weigh on the FTSE's dollar earners. Any BoE speakers hinting at a November hike could move gilts and sterling.
- I could not confirm exact release dates for these items from primary sources.
